newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel denies "Egypt needs psychiatrist" report.
newsitem.headline: Israel denies "Egypt needs psychiatrist" report.

text.p: Israel, fearing damage to ties with Cairo, on Friday scrambled to deny a newspaper report quoting its military intelligence chief as saying Egypt needed a psychiatrist to sort out contradictory policies toward Israel.
The Yedioth Ahronoth report came amidst Egyptian efforts to revive Israeli-PLO peace moves, stalled since Israel began building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.

"A statement like 'Egypt needs a psychiatrist' was never made by me," army intelligence chief Moshe Yaalon told Israel's army radio. "And obviously it is damaging to the question of the State of Israel's foreign affairs."
"To my regret I find myself, not for the first time, coping with incorrect, inaccurate quotes in the media of things or analyses said by me or my people in closed forums," he said.

Army and Israel Radio stations both said that at the weekly cabinet session Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai took the "extraordinary" step of requesting at the start of the meeting to make a statement denying the report.

"In his words the report was a serious attempt to damage the head of army intelligence, army intelligence, and Israel's ties with Egypt," army radio said of Mordechai's statement. Mordechai's spokesman was not available to comment.
Army radio said Mordechai hinted that the source of the report was sitting in the cabinet room.
The daily Yedioth Ahronoth said on Friday that a government source who was present at discussions with Yaalon quoted the intelligence head as saying: "Egypt is a state that needs a psychiatrist".

Yaalon was quoted as saying Egypt -- which in 1979 became the first Arab state to make peace with Israel -- had yet to decide to adopt the peaceful approach of its late President Anwar Sadat or the hostile line of his predecessor Gamal Abdel Nasser toward Israel.
